arXiv:1806.00524v2 [math.CA] 09 Oct 2018

Inequalities for some integrals involving modified Bessel functions

Robert E. Gaunt Note: School of Mathematics, The University of Manchester, Manchester M13 9PL, UK
August 24, 2026
Abstract

Simple inequalities are established for some integrals involving the modified Bessel functions of the first and second kind. In most cases these inequalities are tight in certain limits. As a consequence, we deduce a tight double inequality, involving the modified Bessel function of the first kind, for a generalized hypergeometric function. We also present some open problems that arise from this research.

Keywords: Modified Bessel function; inequality; integral

AMS 2010 Subject Classification: Primary 33C10; 26D15

1 Introduction

In the recent papers [7] and [8], simple inequalities, involving modified Bessel functions of the first kind Iν​(x)I_{\nu}(x) and second kind Kν​(x)K_{\nu}(x), were obtained for the integrals

∫0xe−γ​t​tν​Iν​(t)​𝑑t,∫x∞eγ​t​tν​Kν​(t)​𝑑t,\int_{0}^{x}\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma t}t^{\nu}I_{\nu}(t)\,\mathrm{d}t,\qquad\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}t^{\nu}K_{\nu}(t)\,\mathrm{d}t, (1.1)

where x>0x>0, 0≤γ<10\leq\gamma<1 and ν>−12\nu>-\frac{1}{2}. For γ≠0\gamma\not=0 there does not exist simple closed form expressions for these integrals. Similar inequalities for integrals involving the modified Struve function of the first kind 𝐋ν​(x)\mathbf{L}_{\nu}(x) have also been established by [9]. The bounds of [7, 8] were required in the development of Stein’s method [21, 4, 15] for variance-gamma approximation [5, 6, 10]. Although, the combination of their simple form and accuracy mean that the inequalities may also prove useful in other problems involving modified Bessel functions; see, for example, [2, 3] in which inequalities for the modified Bessel function of the first kind are used to obtain tight bounds for the generalized Marcum Q-function, which frequently arises in radar signal processing.

In this paper, we consider the problem of obtaining inequalities, involving modified Bessel functions, for the integrals

∫0xe−γ​t​Iν​(t)tν​𝑑t,∫x∞eγ​t​Kν​(t)tν​𝑑t,\int_{0}^{x}\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma t}\frac{I_{\nu}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t,\qquad\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\frac{K_{\nu}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t, (1.2)

where x>0x>0 and 0≤γ<10\leq\gamma<1. The conditions imposed on ν\nu will be different for several of the inequalities. (In fact, most of our inequalities are for integrals of a more general form.) This is a related problem to the one considered by [7, 8], and, as is the case for the integrals of (1.1), it is natural to consider such integrals. Indeed, several related integrals are tabulated in standard references. For example, formulas 10.43.8 and 10.43.10 of [14] are

∫0xe−t​Iν​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{0}^{x}\mathrm{e}^{-t}\frac{I_{\nu}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t =2−ν+1(2​ν−1)​Γ​(ν)−e−x​x−ν+12​ν−1​(Iν​(x)+Iν−1​(x)),ν∉{12}∪−ℕ0,\displaystyle=\frac{2^{-\nu+1}}{(2\nu-1)\Gamma(\nu)}-\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-x}x^{-\nu+1}}{2\nu-1}\big(I_{\nu}(x)+I_{\nu-1}(x)\big),\quad\nu\notin\{\tfrac{1}{2}\}\cup-\mathbb{N}_{0},
∫x∞et​Kν​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{t}\frac{K_{\nu}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t =ex​x−ν+12​ν−1​(Kν​(x)+Kν−1​(x)),ν>12.\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{e}^{x}x^{-\nu+1}}{2\nu-1}\big(K_{\nu}(x)+K_{\nu-1}(x)\big),\quad\nu>\tfrac{1}{2}.

When γ=0\gamma=0 the integrals in (1.2) can also be evaluated because the modified Bessel functions can be represented through the generalized hypergeometric function. To see this, recall that the generalized hypergeometric function (see [14]) is defined by

Fqp​(a1,…,ap,b1,…,bq,x)=∑k=0∞(a1)k⋯(ap)k(b1)k⋯(bq)k​xkk!,{}_{p}F_{q}\big(a_{1},\ldots,a_{p};b_{1},\ldots,b_{q};x\big)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(a_{1})_{k}\cdots(a_{p})_{k}}{(b_{1})_{k}\cdots(b_{q})_{k}}\frac{x^{k}}{k!},

and the Pochhammer symbol is given by (a)0=1(a)_{0}=1 and (a)k=a(a+1)(a+2)⋯(a+k−1)(a)_{k}=a(a+1)(a+2)\cdots(a+k-1), k≥1k\geq 1. The modified Bessel functions can be defined for x>0x>0 and ν∈ℝ\nu\in\mathbb{R} by

Iν​(x)=∑k=0∞(12​x)ν+2​kk!​Γ​(ν+k+1),Kν​(x)=π2​sin⁡(ν​π)​(I−ν​(x)−Iν​(x)),I_{\nu}(x)=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\frac{(\frac{1}{2}x)^{\nu+2k}}{k!\Gamma(\nu+k+1)},\qquad K_{\nu}(x)=\frac{\pi}{2\sin(\nu\pi)}\big(I_{-\nu}(x)-I_{\nu}(x)\big), (1.3)

where for Kν​(x)K_{\nu}(x) a limit is taken for integer ν\nu. We then have the representation (see formula 10.39.9 of [14])

Iν​(x)=(12​x)νΓ⁡(ν+1)​F10​(−,ν+1,x24),I_{\nu}(x)=\frac{(\frac{1}{2}x)^{\nu}}{\Gamma(\nu+1)}{}_{0}F_{1}\bigg(-;\nu+1;\frac{x^{2}}{4}\bigg),

and straightforward calculations then yield

∫Iν​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int\frac{I_{\nu}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t =x2ν​Γ​(ν+1)​F21​(12,32,ν+1,x24),\displaystyle=\frac{x}{2^{\nu}\Gamma(\nu+1)}{}_{1}F_{2}\bigg(\frac{1}{2};\frac{3}{2},\nu+1;\frac{x^{2}}{4}\bigg), (1.4)
∫Kν​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int\frac{K_{\nu}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t =−π​x2ν+1​sin⁡(π​ν){4ν​x−2​ν(2​ν−1)​Γ​(1−ν)F21(12−ν;32−ν,1−ν;x24)\displaystyle=-\frac{\pi x}{2^{\nu+1}\sin(\pi\nu)}\bigg\{\frac{4^{\nu}x^{-2\nu}}{(2\nu-1)\Gamma(1-\nu)}{}_{1}F_{2}\bigg(\frac{1}{2}-\nu;\frac{3}{2}-\nu,1-\nu;\frac{x^{2}}{4}\bigg)
+1Γ⁡(ν+1)F21(12;32,ν+1;x24)}.\displaystyle\quad+\frac{1}{\Gamma(\nu+1)}{}_{1}F_{2}\bigg(\frac{1}{2};\frac{3}{2},\nu+1;\frac{x^{2}}{4}\bigg)\bigg\}. (1.5)

However, when γ≠0\gamma\not=0 there does not exist closed form formulas for the integrals in (1.2). Moreover, even when γ=0\gamma=0 the integrals are given in terms of the generalized hypergeometric function. This provides the motivation for establishing simple bounds, involving modified Bessel functions, for these integrals.

The approach used in this paper to bound the integrals in (1.2), which involves exploiting basic identities and monotonicity properties of modified Bessel functions, is similar to the one used in [7, 8]. These elementary properties of modified Bessel functions are collected in Appendix B. In Appendix A, we prove an inequality involving the modified Bessel function Kν​(x)K_{\nu}(x) that is needed to prove one of our integral inequalities. This result may be of independent interest. The inequalities obtained in this paper are simple, but, in most cases, are seen to be tight in certain limits.

2 Inequalities for integrals of modified Bessel functions

The following theorem complements the inequalities of Theorem 2.5 of [7] and Theorem 2.2 of [8] for the integral ∫x∞eγ​t​tν​Kν​(t)​𝑑t\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}t^{\nu}K_{\nu}(t)\,\mathrm{d}t.

Theorem 2.1.

Let 0<γ<10<\gamma<1 and n<1n<1. Then, for all x>0x>0,

∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t >Kν+n−2​(x)xν,ν>52−2​n,\displaystyle>\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{x^{\nu}},\quad\nu>\tfrac{5}{2}-2n, (2.6)
∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t <Kν+n−1​(x)xν,ν∈ℝ,\displaystyle<\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}},\quad\nu\in\mathbb{R}, (2.7)
∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t <2​(ν+n−1)2​ν+n−1​Kν+n−1​(x)xν−n−12​ν+n−1​Kν+n−3​(x)xν,\displaystyle<\frac{2(\nu+n-1)}{2\nu+n-1}\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}-\frac{n-1}{2\nu+n-1}\frac{K_{\nu+n-3}(x)}{x^{\nu}}, (2.8)
                   for ν>12​(1−n)\nu>\tfrac{1}{2}(1-n).
∫x∞eγ​t​Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t <eγ​x1−γ​∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t,ν≥12−n,\displaystyle<\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\gamma x}}{1-\gamma}\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t,\quad\nu\geq\tfrac{1}{2}-n, (2.9)
∫x∞eγ​t​Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t <eγ​x1−γ​Kν+n−1​(x)xν,ν≥12−n,\displaystyle<\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\gamma x}}{1-\gamma}\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}},\quad\nu\geq\tfrac{1}{2}-n, (2.10)
∫x∞eγ​t​Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t <eγ​x1−γ​(2​(ν+n−1)2​ν+n−1​Kν+n−1​(x)xν−n−12​ν+n−1​Kν+n−3​(x)xν),\displaystyle<\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\gamma x}}{1-\gamma}\bigg(\frac{2(\nu+n-1)}{2\nu+n-1}\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}-\frac{n-1}{2\nu+n-1}\frac{K_{\nu+n-3}(x)}{x^{\nu}}\bigg), (2.11)
                   for ν>12​(1−n)\nu>\tfrac{1}{2}(1-n).

Inequality (2.7) is reversed when n>1n>1 and equality is attained when n=1n=1. Equality is attained in (2.9) and (2.10) when n=1n=1 and ν=−12\nu=-\tfrac{1}{2}, and the inequalities are reversed if n>1n>1 and ν≤12−n\nu\leq\frac{1}{2}-n. Inequalities (2.6)–(2.11) are tight as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty. Inequality (2.8) is also tight as x↓0x\downarrow 0, provided ν>1−n\nu>1-n.

Proof.

We first establish inequalities (2.6)–(2.11) and then prove that the inequalities are tight in certain limits.

(i) Let us first compare the derivatives of ∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t and Kν+n−2​(x)xν\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{x^{\nu}}. From the differentiation formula (B.38) and identity (B.36) we have

dd​x​(Kν+n−2​(x)xν)\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\bigg(\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{x^{\nu}}\bigg) =dd​x​(xn−2⋅Kν+n−2​(x)xν+n−2)=(n−2)​Kν+n−2​(x)xν+1−Kν+n−1​(x)xν\displaystyle=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\bigg(x^{n-2}\cdot\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{x^{\nu+n-2}}\bigg)=(n-2)\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{x^{\nu+1}}-\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}
=n−22​(ν+n−2)​(Kν+n−1​(x)xν−Kν+n−3​(x)xν)−Kν+n−1​(x)xν\displaystyle=\frac{n-2}{2(\nu+n-2)}\bigg(\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}-\frac{K_{\nu+n-3}(x)}{x^{\nu}}\bigg)-\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}
=−2​ν+n−22​(ν+n−2)​Kν+n−1​(x)xν+2−n2​(ν+n−2)​Kν+n−3​(x)xν\displaystyle=-\frac{2\nu+n-2}{2(\nu+n-2)}\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}+\frac{2-n}{2(\nu+n-2)}\frac{K_{\nu+n-3}(x)}{x^{\nu}} (2.12)
>−Kν+n​(x)xν=dd​x​(∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t),\displaystyle>-\frac{K_{\nu+n}(x)}{x^{\nu}}=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\bigg(\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t\bigg), (2.13)

where the inequality follows from Lemma A.1. Thus, ∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t decays at a faster rate than Kν+n−2​(x)xν\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{x^{\nu}} for all x>0x>0.

We now consider the asymptotic behaviour of ∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t and Kν+n−2​(x)xν\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{x^{\nu}} as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty. To this end, we note that a routine asymptotic analysis using integration by parts gives that, as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty,

∫x∞t−ν−1/2​e−t​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}t^{-\nu-1/2}\mathrm{e}^{-t}\,\mathrm{d}t ∼x−ν−1/2​e−x​(1−ν+12x),\displaystyle\sim x^{-\nu-1/2}\mathrm{e}^{-x}\bigg(1-\frac{\nu+\tfrac{1}{2}}{x}\bigg),
∫x∞t−ν−3/2​e−t​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}t^{-\nu-3/2}\mathrm{e}^{-t}\,\mathrm{d}t ∼x−ν−3/2​e−x.\displaystyle\sim x^{-\nu-3/2}\mathrm{e}^{-x}.

Using (B.42) and these limiting forms gives that, as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty,

∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t ∼π2​∫x∞t−ν−1/2​e−t​(1+4​(ν+n)2−18​t)​𝑑t\displaystyle\sim\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}}\int_{x}^{\infty}t^{-\nu-1/2}\mathrm{e}^{-t}\bigg(1+\frac{4(\nu+n)^{2}-1}{8t}\bigg)\,\mathrm{d}t
∼π2​x−ν−1/2​e−x​(1+4​(ν+n)2−8​ν−58​x).\displaystyle\sim\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}}x^{-\nu-1/2}\mathrm{e}^{-x}\bigg(1+\frac{4(\nu+n)^{2}-8\nu-5}{8x}\bigg). (2.14)

We also have, as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty,

Kν+n−2​(x)xν∼π2​x−ν−1/2​e−x​(1+4​(ν+n−2)2−18​x).\displaystyle\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{x^{\nu}}\sim\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}}x^{-\nu-1/2}\mathrm{e}^{-x}\bigg(1+\frac{4(\nu+n-2)^{2}-1}{8x}\bigg). (2.15)

One can readily check that the second term in the expansion (2.14) is greater than the second term in the expansion (2.15) if ν>52−2​n\nu>\frac{5}{2}-2n. Combining this with (2.13) then proves inequality (2.6).

(ii) Suppose n<1n<1. Then, for x>0x>0,

∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t=∫x∞tn−1⋅Kν+n​(t)tν+n−1​𝑑t<xn−1​∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν+n−1​𝑑t=Kν+n−1​(x)xν,\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t=\int_{x}^{\infty}t^{n-1}\cdot\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu+n-1}}\,\mathrm{d}t<x^{n-1}\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu+n-1}}\,\mathrm{d}t=\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}},

where we used (B.38) to evaluate the integral. We can see that we have equality if n=1n=1 and the inequality is reversed if n>1n>1.

(iii) From (2.12), we have

dd​t​(Kν+n−1​(t)tν)=−2​ν+n−12​(ν+n−1)​Kν+n​(t)tν−n−12​(ν+n−1)​Kν+n−2​(t)tν.\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\bigg(\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\bigg)=-\frac{2\nu+n-1}{2(\nu+n-1)}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}-\frac{n-1}{2(\nu+n-1)}\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(t)}{t^{\nu}}.

Integrating both sides of this expression over (x,∞)(x,\infty), applying the fundamental theorem of calculus and rearranging gives

∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t=2​(ν+n−1)2​ν+n−1​Kν+n−1​(x)xν−n−12​ν+n−1​∫x∞Kν+n−2​(t)tν​𝑑t.\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t=\frac{2(\nu+n-1)}{2\nu+n-1}\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}-\frac{n-1}{2\nu+n-1}\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t.

On applying inequality (2.7) to the integral on the right hand-side of the above expression we obtain (2.8).

(iv) Suppose n<1n<1 and ν≥12−n\nu\geq\tfrac{1}{2}-n. Using integration by parts gives

∫x∞eγ​t​Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t =eγ​x​∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t+γ​∫x∞eγ​t​(∫t∞Kν+n​(u)uν​𝑑u)​𝑑t\displaystyle=\mathrm{e}^{\gamma x}\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t+\gamma\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\bigg(\int_{t}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(u)}{u^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}u\bigg)\,\mathrm{d}t
<eγ​x​∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t+γ​∫x∞eγ​t​Kν+n−1​(t)tν​𝑑t\displaystyle<\mathrm{e}^{\gamma x}\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t+\gamma\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t
≤eγ​x​∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t+γ​∫x∞eγ​t​Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t,\displaystyle\leq\mathrm{e}^{\gamma x}\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t+\gamma\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t,

where we used (2.7) and (B.45) (as ν≥12−n\nu\geq\frac{1}{2}-n) to obtain the first and second inequalities respectively. Rearranging yields inequality (2.9). If n=1n=1, then the strict inequality in the above expression because an equality. If also ν=−12\nu=-\frac{1}{2}, then the final inequality becomes an equality. Therefore if n=1n=1 and ν=−12\nu=-\frac{1}{2} then (2.9) is an equality. Similar considerations, using (B.44), show that (2.9) is reversed if n>1n>1 and ν≤12−n\nu\leq\frac{1}{2}-n.

(v) Combine inequalities (2.9) and (2.7).

(vi) Combine inequalities (2.9) and (2.8).

(vii) To see that inequalities (2.6)–(2.11) are tight as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty, we first note that using the limiting form (B.42) followed by a straightforward asymptotic analysis gives that, for 0≤γ<10\leq\gamma<1, n∈ℝn\in\mathbb{R} and ν∈ℝ\nu\in\mathbb{R},

∫x∞eγ​t​Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t∼π2​∫x∞t−ν−1/2​e−(1−γ)​t​𝑑t∼π2​11−γ​x−ν−1/2​e−(1−γ)​x,\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t\sim\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}}\int_{x}^{\infty}t^{-\nu-1/2}\mathrm{e}^{-(1-\gamma)t}\,\mathrm{d}t\sim\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{1}{1-\gamma}x^{-\nu-1/2}\mathrm{e}^{-(1-\gamma)x},

as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty. As an example, inequality (2.10) is tight as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty because in this limit we also have

eγ​x1−γ​Kν+n−1​(x)xν∼π2​11−γ​x−ν−1/2​e−(1−γ)​x,\frac{\mathrm{e}^{\gamma x}}{1-\gamma}\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}\sim\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2}}\frac{1}{1-\gamma}x^{-\nu-1/2}\mathrm{e}^{-(1-\gamma)x},

and the tightness of the other inequalities is established similarly.

Establishing that inequality (2.8) is tight as x↓0x\downarrow 0, provided ν>1−n\nu>1-n (which we now assume from here on), is a little more involved. We first find a limiting form for the integral in the limit x↓0x\downarrow 0. Suppose that 0<x≪y≪10<x\ll y\ll 1. We may write

∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t=∫xyKν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t+∫y∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t=:J1+J2.\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t=\int_{x}^{y}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{y}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t=:J_{1}+J_{2}.

Then, from the limiting form (B.41), we have

J1∼∫xy2ν+n−1​Γ​(ν+n)​t−2​ν−n​𝑑t\displaystyle J_{1}\sim\int_{x}^{y}2^{\nu+n-1}\Gamma(\nu+n)t^{-2\nu-n}\,\mathrm{d}t =2ν+n−1​Γ​(ν+n)2​ν+n−1​(x−2​ν−n+1+y−2​ν−n+1)\displaystyle=\frac{2^{\nu+n-1}\Gamma(\nu+n)}{2\nu+n-1}\big(x^{-2\nu-n+1}+y^{-2\nu-n+1}\big)
∼2ν+n−1​Γ​(ν+n)2​ν+n−1​x−2​ν−n+1,\displaystyle\sim\frac{2^{\nu+n-1}\Gamma(\nu+n)}{2\nu+n-1}x^{-2\nu-n+1},

and, on using inequality (2.7) to bound the integral,

J2=∫y∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t<Kν+n−1​(y)yν≪Kν+n−1​(x)xν∼2ν+n−2​Γ​(ν+n−1)x2​ν+n−1.\displaystyle J_{2}=\int_{y}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t<\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(y)}{y^{\nu}}\ll\frac{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}\sim\frac{2^{\nu+n-2}\Gamma(\nu+n-1)}{x^{2\nu+n-1}}.

Therefore J2≪J1J_{2}\ll J_{1}, and we have

∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t∼2ν+n−1​Γ​(ν+n)2​ν+n−1​x−2​ν−n+1.\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t\sim\frac{2^{\nu+n-1}\Gamma(\nu+n)}{2\nu+n-1}x^{-2\nu-n+1}.

But, from (B.41) and the standard formula u​Γ​(u)=Γ⁡(u+1)u\Gamma(u)=\Gamma(u+1), we also have

Remark 2.2.

Inequality (2.9) bounds the integral ∫x∞eγ​t​Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\int_{x}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t in terms of the easier to bound integral ∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t. In this way inequality (2.9) is used to deduce inequalities (2.10) and (2.11) from inequalities (2.7) and (2.8). Thus, inequality (2.9) is more accurate than inequalities (2.10) and (2.11), but suffers from taking a more complicated form. A similar comment applies to inequalities (2.22) and (2.23) of Theorem 2.6 below.

Also, it is worth noting that, due to the positivity of Kν​(x)K_{\nu}(x) for x>0x>0 and ν∈ℝ\nu\in\mathbb{R}, inequality (2.8) outperforms inequality (2.7) if n−12​ν+n−1>0\frac{n-1}{2\nu+n-1}>0, with the reverse being true if n−12​ν+n−1<0\frac{n-1}{2\nu+n-1}<0. A similar comparison can be made between inequalities (2.10) and (2.11).

Arguing similarly to we did in part (vii) of the proof of Theorem 2.1, we have, as x↓0x\downarrow 0

Here the limiting form does not involve γ\gamma, and inequality (2.11) is thus not tight as x↓0x\downarrow 0. This is in contrast to inequality (2.8), which can be obtained by setting γ=0\gamma=0 in (2.11).

Now let γ>0\gamma>0 (note that here we are not imposing that γ<1\gamma<1). Then we can use the fact that eγ​t\mathrm{e}^{\gamma t} is an increasing function of tt to obtain from inequality (2.6) that, for x>0x>0,

This author believes that inequality(2.6) can be improved to ∫x∞Kν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t>Kν+n−βν,n​(x)xν\int_{x}^{\infty}\frac{K_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t>\frac{K_{\nu+n-\beta_{\nu,n}}(x)}{x^{\nu}}, where βν,n<2\beta_{\nu,n}<2 for ν>52−2​n\nu>\frac{5}{2}-2n, n<1n<1. Let n<1n<1. For ν≥1−n+2​(1−n)\nu\geq 1-n+\sqrt{2(1-n)}, define αν,n:=ν+n−(ν+n)2−2​ν−1\alpha_{\nu,n}:=\nu+n-\sqrt{(\nu+n)^{2}-2\nu-1}. Then, for all x>0x>0,

It now remains to prove that inequality (2.21) is tight as x↓0x\downarrow 0. From (B.39), we have on the one hand, as x↓0x\downarrow 0,

and on the other,

2​(ν+n+1)n+1​Iν+n+1​(x)xν−2​ν+n+1n+1​Iν+n+3​(x)xν∼xn+12ν+n​(n+1)​Γ​(ν+n+1),\displaystyle\frac{2(\nu+n+1)}{n+1}\frac{I_{\nu+n+1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}-\frac{2\nu+n+1}{n+1}\frac{I_{\nu+n+3}(x)}{x^{\nu}}\sim\frac{x^{n+1}}{2^{\nu+n}(n+1)\Gamma(\nu+n+1)},

where we used that u​Γ​(u)=Γ⁡(u+1)u\Gamma(u)=\Gamma(u+1). This proves the claim. ∎

Remark 2.7.

When n=0n=0 a direct comparison can be made between inequalities (2.19) and (2.20), which we denote by lν(1)​(x)l_{\nu}^{(1)}(x) and lν(2)​(x)l_{\nu}^{(2)}(x), respectively. Applying (B.39), we have that, as x↓0x\downarrow 0,

lν(1)​(x)∼x22ν+2​Γ​(ν+2)andlν(2)​(x)∼x2ν+1​Γ​(ν+2),l_{\nu}^{(1)}(x)\sim\frac{x^{2}}{2^{\nu+2}\Gamma(\nu+2)}\quad\text{and}\quad l_{\nu}^{(2)}(x)\sim\frac{x}{2^{\nu+1}\Gamma(\nu+2)},

whilst applying (B.40) gives that, as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty,

lν(1)​(x)∼ex2​π​x​(1−4​ν2−18​x)andlν(2)​(x)∼ex2​π​x​(1−4​(ν+1)2−18​x).l_{\nu}^{(1)}(x)\sim\frac{\mathrm{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{2\pi x}}\bigg(1-\frac{4\nu^{2}-1}{8x}\bigg)\quad\text{and}\quad l_{\nu}^{(2)}(x)\sim\frac{\mathrm{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{2\pi x}}\bigg(1-\frac{4(\nu+1)^{2}-1}{8x}\bigg).

Thus, for all ν>−12\nu>-\frac{1}{2}, lν(2)​(x)l_{\nu}^{(2)}(x) outperforms lν(1)​(x)l_{\nu}^{(1)}(x) as x↓0x\downarrow 0, whereas lν(1)​(x)l_{\nu}^{(1)}(x) outperforms lν(2)​(x)l_{\nu}^{(2)}(x) as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty.

Inequality (2.19) also serves an important role in the proof of inequality (2.22), and consequently inequality (2.23). This is because the bound lν(1)​(x)l_{\nu}^{(1)}(x) is given in terms of the modified Bessel function Iν​(x)I_{\nu}(x), whereas lν(2)​(x)l_{\nu}^{(2)}(x) is given in terms of Iν+1​(x)I_{\nu+1}(x).

The constants Cν,nC_{\nu,n} can be computed numerically. As an example, we used Mathematica to find C0,0=1.266C_{0,0}=1.266, C1,0=1.682C_{1,0}=1.682 C3,0=2.285C_{3,0}=2.285, C5,0=2.754C_{5,0}=2.754 and C10,0=3.670C_{10,0}=3.670.

Remark 2.9.

The upper bounds (2.24) and (2.25) are not tight in the limits x↓0x\downarrow 0 and x→∞x\rightarrow\infty, but they are of the correct order in both limits (O⁡(xn+1)O(x^{n+1}) as x↓0x\downarrow 0, and O⁡(x−ν−1/2​e(1−γ)​x)O(x^{-\nu-1/2}\mathrm{e}^{(1-\gamma)x}) as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty). The bounds are simple in that they are given in terms of modified Bessel functions of the first kind and a constant Cν,nC_{\nu,n} that can bounded above by 2​(ν+n+1)2(\nu+n+1) or computed numerically as in Remark 2.8 if improved accuracy is required. Whilst for improved accuracy the constant Cν,nC_{\nu,n} needs to be computed numerically for particular values of ν\nu and nn, once this has been done one has a simple bound on the integral ∫0xe−γ​t​Iν+n​(t)tν​𝑑t\int_{0}^{x}\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma t}\frac{I_{\nu+n}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t, for fixed ν\nu and nn, that holds for all x>0x>0. However, the bounds are are not entirely satisfactory in that they only hold for 0<γ<1Cν,n0<\gamma<\frac{1}{C_{\nu,n}}, whereas one would like the inequalities to be valid for all 0<γ<10<\gamma<1. It should be mentioned that a similar problem was encountered by [8] in that the upper bounds obtained for ∫0xe−γ​t​tν​Iν​(t)​𝑑t\int_{0}^{x}\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma t}t^{\nu}I_{\nu}(t)\,\mathrm{d}t where only valid for 0<γ<αν0<\gamma<\alpha_{\nu}, for some 0<αν<10<\alpha_{\nu}<1. The open problem below, which is analogous to Open Problem 2.10 of [8], is considered by this author to be interesting.

Open Problem 2.10.

Find a constant Mν,γ>0M_{\nu,\gamma}>0 such that, for all x>0x>0,

∫0xe−γ​t​Iν​(t)tν​𝑑t<Mν,γ​e−γ​x​Iν+1​(x)xν,ν>−12, 0<γ<1.\int_{0}^{x}\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma t}\frac{I_{\nu}(t)}{t^{\nu}}\,\mathrm{d}t<M_{\nu,\gamma}\mathrm{e}^{-\gamma x}\frac{I_{\nu+1}(x)}{x^{\nu}},\quad\nu>-\tfrac{1}{2},\>0<\gamma<1.

We end by noting that one can combine the inequalities of Theorems 2.1 and 2.6 and the integral formulas (1.4) and (1.5) to obtain lower and upper bounds for a generalized hypergeometric function. We give an example in the following corollary.

Corollary 2.11.

Let ν>12\nu>\frac{1}{2}. Then, for all x>0x>0,

Iν​(x)<xν2ν−1​Γ​(ν)​F21​(12,32,ν,x24)<2​ν​Iν​(x)−(2​ν−1)​Iν+2​(x).I_{\nu}(x)<\frac{x^{\nu}}{2^{\nu-1}\Gamma(\nu)}{}_{1}F_{2}\bigg(\frac{1}{2};\frac{3}{2},\nu;\frac{x^{2}}{4}\bigg)<2\nu I_{\nu}(x)-(2\nu-1)I_{\nu+2}(x). (2.29)

Remark 2.12.

We know from Theorem 2.1 that the two-sided inequality (2.29) is tight in the limit x→∞x\rightarrow\infty, and the upper bound is also tight as x↓0x\downarrow 0. To elaborate further, we denote by Fν​(x)F_{\nu}(x) the expression involving the generalized hypergeometric function in (2.29), and the lower and upper bounds by Lν​(x)L_{\nu}(x) and Uν​(x)U_{\nu}(x). We now note the bound Iν+1​(x)Iν​(x)>x2​(ν+1)+x\frac{I_{\nu+1}(x)}{I_{\nu}(x)}>\frac{x}{2(\nu+1)+x}, ν>−1\nu>-1, which is the simplest lower bound of a sequence of more complicated rational lower bounds given in [17]. We thus obtain that the relative error in approximating Fν​(x)F_{\nu}(x) by either Lν​(x)L_{\nu}(x) or Uν​(x)U_{\nu}(x) is at most

2​ν​Iν​(x)−(2​ν−1)​Iν+2​(x)Iν​(x)−1\displaystyle\frac{2\nu I_{\nu}(x)-(2\nu-1)I_{\nu+2}(x)}{I_{\nu}(x)}-1 =(2​ν−1)​(1−Iν+2​(x)Iν+1​(x)​Iν+1​(x)Iν​(x))\displaystyle=(2\nu-1)\bigg(1-\frac{I_{\nu+2}(x)}{I_{\nu+1}(x)}\frac{I_{\nu+1}(x)}{I_{\nu}(x)}\bigg)
<(2​ν−1)​(1−x2(2​(ν+2)+x)​(2​(ν+1)+x))\displaystyle<(2\nu-1)\bigg(1-\frac{x^{2}}{(2(\nu+2)+x)(2(\nu+1)+x)}\bigg)
=(2​ν−1)​(4​(ν+1)​(ν+2)+(4​ν+6)​x)(2​(ν+1)+x)​(2​(ν+2)+x),\displaystyle=\frac{(2\nu-1)(4(\nu+1)(\nu+2)+(4\nu+6)x)}{(2(\nu+1)+x)(2(\nu+2)+x)},

which, for fixed xx, has rate ν\nu as ν→∞\nu\rightarrow\infty and, for fixed ν\nu, has rate x−1x^{-1} as x→∞x\rightarrow\infty.

We used Mathematica to compute the relative error in approximating Fν​(x)F_{\nu}(x) by Lν​(x)L_{\nu}(x) and Uν​(x)U_{\nu}(x), and numerical results are given in Tables 1 and 2. We observe that, for a given xx, the relative error in approximating Fν​(x)F_{\nu}(x) by either Lν​(x)L_{\nu}(x) or Uν​(x)U_{\nu}(x) increases as ν\nu increases. We also notice from Table 1 that, for a given ν\nu, the relative error in approximating Fν​(x)F_{\nu}(x) by Lν​(x)L_{\nu}(x) decreases as xx increases. However, from Table 2 we see that, for a given ν\nu, as xx increases the relative error in approximating Fν​(x)F_{\nu}(x) by Uν​(x)U_{\nu}(x) initially increases before decreasing. This is because the upper bound is tight as x↓0x\downarrow 0.

−(x−2​(ν+n))2​(x2+(ν+n−12)2)\displaystyle\quad-(x-2(\nu+n))^{2}(x^{2}+(\nu+n-\tfrac{1}{2})^{2})

=2​(ν+n−2)​(Kν+n−2​(x)+2​(ν+n−1)x​Kν+n−1​(x))\displaystyle\quad=2(\nu+n-2)\bigg(K_{\nu+n-2}(x)+\frac{2(\nu+n-1)}{x}K_{\nu+n-1}(x)\bigg)

for all x>0x>0. Kν+n−2​(x)Kν+n−1​(x)>x−2​(ν+n−1)x−(2−n).\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}>\frac{x-2(\nu+n-1)}{x-(2-n)}. (A.33)

But Theorem 2 of [19] (see also [18] and [13]) states that, for ν>32−n\nu>\frac{3}{2}-n and x>0x>0,

Kν+n−2​(x)Kν+n−1​(x)>xν+n−3/2+x2+(ν+n−3/2)2.\frac{K_{\nu+n-2}(x)}{K_{\nu+n-1}(x)}>\frac{x}{\nu+n-3/2+\sqrt{x^{2}+(\nu+n-3/2)^{2}}}.

Appendix B Elementary properties of modified Bessel functions

Here we list standard properties of modified Bessel functions that are used throughout this paper. All these formulas can be found in [14], except for the inequalities.

The modified Bessel functions Iν​(x)I_{\nu}(x) and Kν​(x)K_{\nu}(x) are both regular functions of x∈ℝx\in\mathbb{R}. For positive values of xx the functions Iν​(x)I_{\nu}(x) and Kν​(x)K_{\nu}(x) are positive for ν>−1\nu>-1 and all ν∈ℝ\nu\in\mathbb{R}, respectively. The modified Bessel functions satisfy the following identities and differentiation formulas:

K−ν​(x)\displaystyle K_{-\nu}(x) =Kν​(x),\displaystyle=K_{\nu}(x), (B.34)
Iν+1​(x)\displaystyle I_{\nu+1}(x) =Iν−1​(x)−2​νx​Iν​(x),\displaystyle=I_{\nu-1}(x)-\frac{2\nu}{x}I_{\nu}(x), (B.35)
Kν+1​(x)\displaystyle K_{\nu+1}(x) =Kν−1​(x)+2​νx​Kν​(x),\displaystyle=K_{\nu-1}(x)+\frac{2\nu}{x}K_{\nu}(x), (B.36)
dd​x​(Iν​(x)xν)\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\bigg(\frac{I_{\nu}(x)}{x^{\nu}}\bigg) =Iν+1​(x)xν,\displaystyle=\frac{I_{\nu+1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}, (B.37)
dd​x​(Kν​(x)xν)\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}x}\bigg(\frac{K_{\nu}(x)}{x^{\nu}}\bigg) =−Kν+1​(x)xν,\displaystyle=-\frac{K_{\nu+1}(x)}{x^{\nu}}, (B.38)

and have the following asymptotic behaviour:

Iν​(x)\displaystyle I_{\nu}(x) ∼(12​x)νΓ⁡(ν+1)​(1+x24​(ν+1)),x↓0,ν>−1,\displaystyle\sim\frac{(\frac{1}{2}x)^{\nu}}{\Gamma(\nu+1)}\bigg(1+\frac{x^{2}}{4(\nu+1)}\bigg),\quad x\downarrow 0,\>\nu>-1, (B.39)
Iν​(x)\displaystyle I_{\nu}(x) ∼ex2​π​x​(1−4​ν2−18​x),x→∞,ν∈ℝ,\displaystyle\sim\frac{\mathrm{e}^{x}}{\sqrt{2\pi x}}\bigg(1-\frac{4\nu^{2}-1}{8x}\bigg),\quad x\rightarrow\infty,\>\nu\in\mathbb{R}, (B.40)
Kν​(x)\displaystyle K_{\nu}(x) ∼2ν−1​Γ​(ν)​x−ν,x↓0,ν>0,\displaystyle\sim 2^{\nu-1}\Gamma(\nu)x^{-\nu},\quad x\downarrow 0,\>\nu>0, (B.41)
Kν​(x)\displaystyle K_{\nu}(x) ∼π2​x​e−x​(1+4​ν2−18​x),x→∞,ν∈ℝ.\displaystyle\sim\sqrt{\frac{\pi}{2x}}\mathrm{e}^{-x}\bigg(1+\frac{4\nu^{2}-1}{8x}\bigg),\quad x\rightarrow\infty,\>\nu\in\mathbb{R}. (B.42)

Let x>0x>0. Then the following inequalities hold:

Iν​(x)\displaystyle I_{\nu}(x) <Iν−1​(x),ν≥12,\displaystyle<I_{\nu-1}(x),\quad\nu\geq\tfrac{1}{2}, (B.43)
Kν​(x)\displaystyle K_{\nu}(x) ≤Kν−1​(x),ν≤12,\displaystyle\leq K_{\nu-1}(x),\quad\nu\leq\tfrac{1}{2}, (B.44)
Kν​(x)\displaystyle K_{\nu}(x) ≥Kν−1​(x),ν≥12,\displaystyle\geq K_{\nu-1}(x),\quad\nu\geq\tfrac{1}{2}, (B.45)
Kμ​(x)\displaystyle K_{\mu}(x) <Kν​(x),0≤μ<ν.\displaystyle<K_{\nu}(x),\quad 0\leq\mu<\nu. (B.46)

We have equality in (B.44) and (B.45) if and only if ν=12\nu=\frac{1}{2}. Inequalities (B.44) and (B.45) for Kν​(x)K_{\nu}(x) can be found in [11]. Inequality (B.46) is immediate from the integral representation Kν​(x)=∫0∞e−x​cosh⁡(t)​cosh⁡(ν​t)​𝑑tK_{\nu}(x)=\int_{0}^{\infty}\mathrm{e}^{-x\cosh(t)}\cosh(\nu t)\,\mathrm{d}t, x>0x>0, ν∈ℝ\nu\in\mathbb{R}. The inequality for Iν​(x)I_{\nu}(x) can be found in [12] and [16], which extends a result of [20]. A survey of related inequalities for modified Bessel functions is given by [1], and refinements of inequalities (B.43)–(B.45) can be found in [19] and references therein.
